title: Armor Class
text: AC = 10 + Dex modifier, unarmored, adjusted by armor worn, shield (+2), and effects. An attack hits if the attack roll equals or exceeds the target's AC.

title: Attack Rolls
text: Roll d20 + ability modifier + proficiency bonus (if proficient). Meet or beat the target's AC to hit. A natural 1 always misses; a natural 20 always hits and is a critical hit.

title: Advantage and Disadvantage
text: Roll two d20s, use the higher for advantage or the lower for disadvantage. Multiple sources of each don't stack — you still roll only two dice. If you have both advantage and disadvantage, they cancel and you roll normally.

title: Critical Hits
text: A natural 20 on an attack roll is a critical hit: roll all the attack's damage dice twice and add them together, then add modifiers as normal. Only the dice are doubled, not flat bonuses.

title: Cover
text: Half cover: +2 AC and Dex saves. Three-quarters cover: +5 AC and Dex saves. Total cover: can't be targeted directly. Cover is determined by obstacles between attacker and target, not by the target's own body.

title: Opportunity Attack
text: When a hostile creature you can see leaves your reach (without Disengaging or being forced/teleported), you can use your reaction to make one melee attack against it, as it moves.

title: Reactions
text: You get one reaction per round, usable on another creature's turn (e.g. opportunity attacks, some spells). It resets at the start of your turn. Taking a reaction doesn't use your action or movement.

title: Actions in Combat
text: On your turn you get one action, one move (up to your speed), and one reaction (usable off-turn). Standard actions: Attack, Cast a Spell, Dash, Disengage, Dodge, Help, Hide, Ready, Search, Use an Object.

title: Attack (Action)
text: Make one melee or ranged attack. Some features (Extra Attack, certain spells) let you attack more than once when you take this action.

title: Cast a Spell (Action)
text: Casting a spell with a casting time of 1 action uses your action for the turn. See casting time, components, and range for the full requirements to cast.

title: Dash (Action)
text: Gain extra movement equal to your speed for the current turn, after accounting for other effects that alter your speed.

title: Disengage (Action)
text: Your movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks for the rest of the turn.

title: Dodge (Action)
text: Until the start of your next turn, any attack roll against you has disadvantage if you can see the attacker, and you make Dex saves with advantage. You lose this benefit if incapacitated or if your speed drops to 0.

title: Help (Action)
text: Aid another creature's task check (they get advantage on the next relevant ability check before your next turn), or aid an ally's attack against a creature within 5 ft of you (their next attack roll against that target has advantage).

title: Hide (Action)
text: Make a Dexterity (Stealth) check to try to hide from creatures that can't see you clearly and aren't already aware of you. Success sets the DC for others to find you (usually opposed by passive Perception).

title: Ready (Action)
text: Choose a trigger and an action/movement to take in response. On the trigger (even off your turn) you can use your reaction to take that readied action. Costs your action to set up; unused readied actions are lost at the start of your next turn.

title: Search (Action)
text: Devote your attention to finding something — usually a Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation) check.

title: Use an Object (Action)
text: Interact with a second object on your turn beyond the one free object interaction you already get (e.g. drawing a weapon, opening a door is normally free; this covers a second, more involved interaction).

title: Two-Weapon Fighting
text: When you attack with a light melee weapon in one hand, you can use a bonus action to attack with a different light melee weapon in your other hand. Don't add your ability modifier to that bonus-action damage unless it's negative.

title: Ranged Attacks in Melee
text: Making a ranged attack while a hostile creature is within 5 feet of you (and not incapacitated) imposes disadvantage on the attack roll.

title: Grappling
text: In place of one attack, make a Strength (Athletics) check contested by the target's Athletics or Acrobatics. Success: the target is grappled (speed 0) until the grapple ends. Requires a free hand; you can only grapple a creature up to one size larger than you (with help, larger still).

title: Shoving a Creature
text: In place of one attack, make a Strength (Athletics) check contested by the target's Athletics or Acrobatics. Success: knock the target prone, or push it 5 feet away. Same size-limit rule as grappling.

title: Mounted Combat
text: A willing creature at least one size larger, with room, can be mounted using half your movement. You can control a trained mount (it acts on your turn, uses your Dash/Disengage/Help). If the mount is knocked prone or drops to 0 HP, you may fall — a controlled fall costs no reaction, otherwise take fall/prone rules.

title: Underwater Combat
text: Melee attacks have disadvantage unless the attacker has a swim speed or is a water-breather (except with a dagger, javelin, shortsword, spear, or trident). Ranged weapon attacks automatically miss beyond normal range, and have disadvantage even within it, unless the weapon is a crossbow, net, thrown weapon, or javelin/spear/trident/harpoon.

title: Flanking
text: Optional variant rule, not used by default: if you and an ally are on opposite sides of an enemy, both adjacent, you have advantage on melee attacks against it. Check with your table/DM before assuming it's active.

title: Initiative
text: At the start of combat, everyone rolls a Dexterity check (d20 + Dex mod) to set turn order, highest to lowest. Ties are usually broken by the DM or by comparing Dex scores.

title: Movement and Speed
text: Your speed is how many feet you can move per action-equivalent of movement (usually once on your turn, but you can split it around your action). Moving through a hostile creature's space isn't allowed (unless it's two+ sizes different, with a DC 10 Acrobatics/Athletics check to move through).

title: Difficult Terrain
text: Every foot of movement in difficult terrain (rubble, thick undergrowth, deep snow, etc.) costs 1 extra foot, effectively doubling movement cost.

title: Jumping
text: Long jump: with a 10-ft running start, you cover a number of feet up to your Strength score (half that with no running start); each foot costs a foot of movement. High jump: with a running start, 3 + Str modifier feet up (half with no running start), reaching 1/2 that distance out. DM may call for an Athletics check for tricky jumps.

title: Climbing, Swimming, and Crawling
text: Climbing, swimming, and crawling all cost 1 extra foot per foot moved (like difficult terrain), unless you have a climb/swim speed for that mode of movement.

title: Falling Damage
text: 1d6 bludgeoning damage per 10 feet fallen, to a maximum of 20d6, and you land prone (unless damage is somehow negated).

title: Vision and Light
text: Bright light: normal vision. Dim light ("lightly obscured"): Perception checks relying on sight have disadvantage. Darkness ("heavily obscured"): you're effectively blinded in it. Darkvision lets a creature see in dim light as bright and darkness as dim, usually in shades of gray, out to its stated range.

title: Surprise
text: If you're caught unaware at the start of combat (didn't notice a threat), you're surprised: you can't move or take an action/reaction on your first turn, and until that turn ends attacks against you have advantage (Dex saves unaffected). Determined by comparing Stealth to passive Perception before initiative.

title: Hit Points and Damage
text: Damage is subtracted from current HP. At 0 HP (if not already dead outright), a creature falls unconscious and starts making death saving throws; massive damage (a single hit that deals damage equal to or exceeding remaining HP, with excess equal to or more than your HP max) causes instant death instead.

title: Temporary Hit Points
text: A buffer of extra "HP" that absorbs damage before real HP is touched. They don't stack with each other (take the higher value, don't add), can't be healed, and are lost (not restored) at the end of their duration if any is specified.

title: Healing
text: Restored HP can't exceed your hit point maximum; any excess is simply lost. A creature at 0 HP that regains even 1 HP becomes conscious and stops making death saves.

title: Death Saving Throws
text: At 0 HP and not stable, roll d20 at the start of each of your turns (no modifiers): 10+ is a success, below 10 is a failure. Three successes stabilizes you (unconscious at 0 HP); three failures kills you. A natural 20 regains 1 HP instead; a natural 1 counts as two failures. Taking damage while at 0 HP is one automatic failure (two on a crit).

title: Instant Death
text: If damage drops you to 0 HP and there's damage left over equal to or greater than your hit point maximum, you die instantly instead of falling unconscious.

title: Stabilizing a Creature
text: A DC 10 Wisdom (Medicine) check, or a healer's kit use, stabilizes a creature at 0 HP: it stops making death saves but stays unconscious until it regains at least 1 HP.

title: Exhaustion
text: Six cumulative levels, each worse: 1) disadvantage on ability checks; 2) speed halved; 3) disadvantage on attacks and saves; 4) HP max halved; 5) speed reduced to 0; 6) death. A long rest removes one level (with food and water).

title: Short Rest
text: A period of downtime, at least 1 hour, doing nothing more strenuous than eating, reading, or tending wounds. You can spend Hit Dice (roll + Con modifier each) to heal.

title: Long Rest
text: At least 8 hours, with at most 1 hour spent on light activity, interrupted by no more than 1 hour of combat/strenuous activity (which resets it). Restores all HP, regains up to half your total Hit Dice, and removes one exhaustion level. Usable only once per 24 hours.

title: Blinded
text: Can't see, automatically fails sight-based checks. Attack rolls against you have advantage; your attack rolls have disadvantage.

title: Charmed
text: Can't attack the charmer or target it with harmful abilities/spells. The charmer has advantage on social ability checks against you.

title: Deafened
text: Can't hear, automatically fails hearing-based checks.

title: Frightened
text: Disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls while the source of fear is within line of sight. Can't willingly move closer to the source.

title: Grappled (Condition)
text: Speed becomes 0, can't benefit from any bonus to speed. Ends if the grappler is incapacitated, or if you're removed from the grappler's reach by an effect (e.g. a Shove).

title: Incapacitated
text: Can't take actions or reactions.

title: Invisible
text: Can't be seen without special sense; you're heavily obscured for hiding purposes. Attack rolls against you have disadvantage; your attack rolls have advantage. Location can still be detected by noise or tracks.

title: Paralyzed
text: Incapacitated, can't move or speak. Automatically fails Str and Dex saves. Attack rolls against you have advantage, and any hit from within 5 ft is a critical hit.

title: Petrified
text: Transformed (with nonmagical objects worn/carried) into solid substance; incapacitated, can't move or speak, unaware of surroundings. Attack rolls against you have advantage. Automatically fail Str and Dex saves. Resistance to all damage. Immune to poison and disease (existing ones are suspended, not cured).

title: Poisoned
text: Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.

title: Prone
text: Only movement option is to crawl (or stand, ending the condition). Disadvantage on attack rolls. Melee attacks against you have advantage; ranged attacks against you have disadvantage.

title: Restrained
text: Speed becomes 0. Disadvantage on attack rolls and Dex saves. Attack rolls against you have advantage.

title: Stunned
text: Incapacitated, can't move, can speak only falteringly. Automatically fails Str and Dex saves. Attack rolls against you have advantage.

title: Unconscious
text: Incapacitated, can't move or speak, unaware of surroundings, drops what it's holding and falls prone. Automatically fails Str and Dex saves. Attack rolls against you have advantage, and any hit from within 5 ft is a critical hit.

title: Casting Time
text: Most spells take 1 action. Some take a bonus action, a reaction (usually with a specific trigger, e.g. Shield), or longer (minutes/hours). Casting a bonus-action spell restricts you to only cantrips (with a casting time of 1 action) for any other spell that turn.

title: Spell Range
text: The distance the spell can reach from you (feet), or "Touch", "Self", or "Self (radius)" for effects centered on you. You must have a clear path to the target's space to target it, with the usual exceptions for cover.

title: Spell Components (V, S, M)
text: V (Verbal): spoken, so you can't cast if silenced. S (Somatic): requires a free hand for gesturing. M (Material): needs the listed component(s), consumed if a cost is given, otherwise a component pouch/spellcasting focus suffices. Missing a required component means the spell fails.

title: Spell Duration
text: How long the effect lasts: Instantaneous (effect happens and it's done), a stated span of rounds/minutes/hours, or Concentration for as long as you maintain focus (up to a max).

title: Concentration
text: You can concentrate on only one spell at a time — casting another concentration spell ends the first. Taking damage requires a Constitution save (DC 10 or half the damage, whichever is higher) to keep concentrating. Also ends if incapacitated, killed, or you choose to end it.

title: Spell Targets
text: You generally need a clear path to a target (not behind total cover) and, unless the spell says otherwise, must be able to see the target. A spell can target you even if you're not normally allowed to target yourself, if it says "target" without excluding you.

title: Spell Attack Rolls
text: Roll d20 + spellcasting ability modifier + proficiency bonus, same as a weapon attack, compared against the target's AC.

title: Combining Spell Effects
text: The same spell cast multiple times doesn't stack (e.g. two castings of a bonus spell don't add together — the higher/most recent applies per its own rules). Different spells' effects, on the other hand, do combine.

title: Casting in Armor
text: If you're not proficient with the armor (or shield) you're wearing, you can't cast spells while wearing it.

title: Spell Slots
text: Casting a leveled spell expends one slot of that spell's level or higher; slots refresh (fully or partly) on a long rest, depending on class. Casting with a higher slot than the spell's base level often boosts the effect ("at higher levels").

title: Rituals
text: A spell tagged ritual can be cast by taking 10 minutes longer than normal, without expending a spell slot — if you have that spell prepared/known and your class allows ritual casting.

title: Known vs. Prepared Spells
text: "Known" casters (e.g. Sorcerer, Bard) have a fixed spell list they can cast at will (within slots). "Prepared" casters (e.g. Cleric, Wizard, Druid) choose a subset of their available spells after a long rest and can only cast from that day's prepared list.

title: Ability Checks
text: Roll d20 + relevant ability modifier (+ proficiency bonus if proficient in the associated skill) against a DC set by the DM. Represents attempting a task where the outcome is uncertain.

title: Skills
text: Skills tie to specific ability checks (e.g. Stealth uses Dex, Persuasion uses Cha). Proficiency in a skill adds your proficiency bonus; some classes/features grant Expertise, doubling that bonus.

title: Proficiency Bonus
text: Scales with character level (+2 at levels 1–4, up to +6 at levels 17–20). Added to attack rolls with weapons/spells you're proficient with, ability checks for skills/tools you're proficient in, and saving throws you're proficient in.

title: Saving Throws
text: Roll d20 + the relevant ability modifier (+ proficiency bonus if proficient in that save) to resist or reduce an effect. The DC is usually set by whatever caused the effect (e.g. 8 + spellcasting mod + proficiency bonus for a spell save DC).

title: Passive Checks
text: A passive check (usually Perception) = 10 + relevant modifiers, used instead of rolling when there's no immediate pressure — most commonly to see if a character notices something without actively looking.

title: Working Together (Helping)
text: When two or more characters team up on a task, one makes the check while the other(s), if capable of contributing, grant advantage. Only one helper can grant advantage regardless of how many are helping.

title: Group Checks
text: Everyone in the group makes the same ability check; if at least half the group succeeds, the whole group succeeds. Used for things like the whole party sneaking past a guard together.

title: Contests
text: Both sides make opposed ability checks (not necessarily the same skill) with the same DC of each other's roll; higher roll wins, ties mean the status quo is maintained.

title: Carrying Capacity
text: You can carry up to Strength score × 15 lbs. Pushing/dragging/lifting caps out around double that. Exceeding your carrying capacity means you're encumbered (rules vary by table; many groups track this loosely or not at all).

title: Inspiration
text: A DM-awarded reward (usually for good roleplaying) that you can spend for advantage on one attack roll, ability check, or saving throw. You either have it or you don't — it doesn't stack.

title: Weapons
text: Weapons are Simple or Martial, and Melee or Ranged. Your class and background determine which categories you're proficient with — you only add your proficiency bonus to attacks made with weapons you're proficient in.

title: Weapon Properties
text: Ammunition: needs drawn/loaded ammo; recovering it after a fight takes about 1 minute per piece. Finesse: use Str or Dex, your choice, for attack and damage. Heavy: Small creatures have disadvantage using it. Light: eligible for two-weapon fighting. Loading: only one shot per action regardless of extra attacks. Range: normal/long range in feet — beyond normal imposes disadvantage, beyond long you can't hit at all. Reach: adds 5 ft to your reach. Special: has its own extra rule, described with the weapon. Thrown: can be thrown as a ranged attack using the same ability modifier as melee. Two-Handed: requires both hands. Versatile: usable one- or two-handed; the second die is for two-handed use.

title: Club
text: Simple melee. 1d4 bludgeoning. Light.

title: Dagger
text: Simple melee. 1d4 piercing. Finesse, Light, Thrown (range 20/60).

title: Greatclub
text: Simple melee. 1d8 bludgeoning. Two-Handed.

title: Handaxe
text: Simple melee. 1d6 slashing. Light, Thrown (range 20/60).

title: Javelin
text: Simple melee. 1d6 piercing. Thrown (range 30/120).

title: Light Hammer
text: Simple melee. 1d4 bludgeoning. Light, Thrown (range 20/60).

title: Mace
text: Simple melee. 1d6 bludgeoning.

title: Quarterstaff
text: Simple melee. 1d6 bludgeoning. Versatile (1d8).

title: Sickle
text: Simple melee. 1d4 slashing. Light.

title: Spear
text: Simple melee. 1d6 piercing. Thrown (range 20/60), Versatile (1d8).

title: Unarmed Strike
text: 1 bludgeoning damage plus Str modifier (or a class feature's alternative, e.g. a Monk's martial arts die).

title: Light Crossbow
text: Simple ranged. 1d8 piercing. Ammunition (range 80/320), Loading, Two-Handed.

title: Dart
text: Simple ranged. 1d4 piercing. Finesse, Thrown (range 20/60).

title: Shortbow
text: Simple ranged. 1d6 piercing. Ammunition (range 80/320), Two-Handed.

title: Sling
text: Simple ranged. 1d4 bludgeoning. Ammunition (range 30/120).

title: Battleaxe
text: Martial melee. 1d8 slashing. Versatile (1d10).

title: Flail
text: Martial melee. 1d8 bludgeoning.

title: Glaive
text: Martial melee. 1d10 slashing. Heavy, Reach, Two-Handed.

title: Greataxe
text: Martial melee. 1d12 slashing. Heavy, Two-Handed.

title: Greatsword
text: Martial melee. 2d6 slashing. Heavy, Two-Handed.

title: Halberd
text: Martial melee. 1d10 slashing. Heavy, Reach, Two-Handed.

title: Lance
text: Martial melee. 1d12 piercing. Reach, Special (disadvantage against targets within 5 ft; requires two hands unless you're mounted).

title: Longsword
text: Martial melee. 1d8 slashing. Versatile (1d10).

title: Maul
text: Martial melee. 2d6 bludgeoning. Heavy, Two-Handed.

title: Morningstar
text: Martial melee. 1d8 piercing.

title: Pike
text: Martial melee. 1d10 piercing. Heavy, Reach, Two-Handed.

title: Rapier
text: Martial melee. 1d8 piercing. Finesse.

title: Scimitar
text: Martial melee. 1d6 slashing. Finesse, Light.

title: Shortsword
text: Martial melee. 1d6 piercing. Finesse, Light.

title: Trident
text: Martial melee. 1d6 piercing. Thrown (range 20/60), Versatile (1d8).

title: War Pick
text: Martial melee. 1d8 piercing.

title: Warhammer
text: Martial melee. 1d8 bludgeoning. Versatile (1d10).

title: Whip
text: Martial melee. 1d4 slashing. Finesse, Reach.

title: Blowgun
text: Martial ranged. 1 piercing. Ammunition (range 25/100), Loading.

title: Hand Crossbow
text: Martial ranged. 1d6 piercing. Ammunition (range 30/120), Light, Loading.

title: Heavy Crossbow
text: Martial ranged. 1d10 piercing. Ammunition (range 100/400), Heavy, Loading, Two-Handed.

title: Longbow
text: Martial ranged. 1d8 piercing. Ammunition (range 150/600), Heavy, Two-Handed.

title: Net
text: Martial ranged. No damage. Special (a Large or smaller creature hit is restrained until freed; DC 10 Str check or 5 slashing damage to break it), Thrown (range 5/15).
